sentences.text:
Salim Lari @ Salim Zafer Lari vs State Of U.P. on 19 October,
2019
Author: Sudhir Agarwal

Bench: Sudhir Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Court No. - 34
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 7 of 1998
Revisionist :- Salim Lari @ Salim Zafer Lari
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- R.B. Sahai
Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.
Heard Sri R.B. Sahai, learned counsel for revisionist and perused the material available on record.

2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by judgement and order dated 20.12.1997 passed by Sri G.S. Nema, IInd Additional Sessions Judge, Deoria, in Criminal Appeal No. 14 of 1992, dismissing appeal and maintaining conviction of appellant but reducing sentence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954") to six months rigorous imprisonment and Rs. 1000/- as fine and in default of payment of fine, he shall suffer further one month's rigorous imprisonment as awarded by Sri Jai Mangal Sharma, learned Judicial Magistrate, Deoria vide judgement and order dated 29.04.1992 in Criminal Case No. 1574 of 1990.
Being aggrieved, appellant has preferred present revision.

1 3.

entities.text: Salim Lari @ Salim Zafer Lari vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that there is no compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954.

A copy of Public Analyst Report was not supplied to revisionist but Trial Court has rejected this contention only on the ground that copy of Public Analyst Report was sent to revisionist by registered post, therefore,
service is deemed sufficient and it is for revisionist to apply for the test of sample from Central Food Laboratory, Calcutta which is not opted by revisionist and the same view has been taken by Appellate Court also which is wholly illegal, inasmuch as, law is now well settled that for compliance of said section, mere sending of notice is not sufficient but prosecution has to prove its service/receipt upon accused.
4.

On the question of compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954, I find that Lower Appellate Court has discussed this issue in para-9 which reads as under:-
"9.

P.W.2 Ashok Kumar- Food Clerk has specifically stated in his statement before the Court below that he sent the Public Analyst Report's coply alongwith the information of launching prosecution against the accused through registered letter to the accused on his given address.
This has not been received back by the Food Clerk so there the only presumption is that it was received by the accused.

The accused should have applied for sending the sample to the Director, Central Food Laboratory,
Calcutta for obtaining the certificate from the Director superseding the Public Analyst's report but he did not opt for so that there is no non-compliance of Section 13(2) of P.F.A. Act.
When the accused has not applied under Section 13(2) of P.F.A.Act, he is not prejudiced.

Hence, the appeal on this count also fails."
5.

From a perusal of above paragraph, it is evident that Court below has treated sufficient compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 when notice along with a copy of Public Analyst report was sent to accused.

However, in my view, service of notice upon accused was necessary to be proved by Prosecution so as to prove compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 and in absence of such evidence,
proceedings are vitiated in law.

I am fortified in taking above view from recent Supreme Court's Judgement in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019. In para 15 of judgment

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, Court has said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.
Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.
In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as Salim Lari @ Salim Zafer Lari vs State Of U.P. on 19 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13104938/
2 per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient."

sentences.text: (emphasis added)
6. In view thereof, application is allowed.
Impugned judgements of Courts below are hereby set aside.
7. Certify the judgment to the Court below immediately.
